name: competitor-posts
description: Judge one competitor post (LinkedIn, Instagram or YouTube) for the B2B service company in creator_profile: topic lane, audience fit, hook, proof, replicable, sponsored, news-pegged.

topic_lane.instructions: What is the main subject of the post, judged from `title` (its first line) first and `description` (the full post text or caption) second?

criteria.method: Teaches a method, framework, checklist, template or step-by-step process that the reader could apply in their own business.
criteria.client_result: Shows a project, case study, launch or measured result the company delivered for a client, or a client testimonial or review.
criteria.market_view: An opinion about the market, industry trends, predictions, pricing in the industry or commentary on news, without a step-by-step method.
criteria.offer_pitch: Describes the company's own services or offer, or invites the reader to book a call, join a webinar, download a resource or apply.
criteria.founder_story: A personal story or lesson of the founder or the team that is tied to running the business: mistakes, decisions, milestones.
criteria.off_niche: Anything else: hiring, team photos, events, holidays, personal life unrelated to business, generic motivation or news unrelated to the company's audience.

icp_fit.instructions: How directly does the post (`title`, `description`) serve the buyers named in `creator_profile` (its ICP segments, their pain points and goals)?
criteria: Off target: gives these buyers nothing to use.
Adjacent: a topic aimed at peers, job seekers or other agencies, with no use for these buyers stated.
On target: shows a method, a warning sign, a checklist or a model these buyers could apply to a problem from `creator_profile`.
Bullseye: names a business outcome for such a buyer (money or time saved, a launch date, revenue, a risk avoided) and the method that produced it.

hook_type.instructions: Which hook pattern opens `title` (the first line of the post)? When two patterns appear, pick the one that appears first in `title`.

criteria.contradiction: Denies a common belief or tells the viewer to stop doing something: stop, don't, is dead, is lying, wrong, nobody tells you.
criteria.number_specific: Leads with a specific number, count, or dollar amount as the draw: 84 skills, $1M, 10x, 3 steps, 7 tools.
criteria.newsjack: Leads with a product, model, or feature presented as new: just dropped, just released, new, a version number.
criteria.outcome_build: Leads with something the creator built or a result they got: I built, how I, my system, I replaced.
criteria.how_to: Leads with an instruction or a tutorial promise: how to, full guide, course, tutorial, setup, step by step.

proof.instructions: How much visible proof does the post give in `description`?
criteria: Opinion, advice or news only: no tool, system or example is shown.
Names a specific tool, template or setup, or tells one concrete example.
Walks through a full system or process step by step, or shares the template itself.
Shows a measured result: money or time saved, load time before and after, launch in N days, revenue, a count.

replicable.instructions: Could the company in `creator_profile` publish its own version of this post with its own projects, numbers and process, without needing the original author's personal story, private data, audience size or a sponsor's product?

sponsored.instructions: Is the whole post a paid promotion or a partnership for one named company's product (marked as sponsored, a brand partnership, a discount code or a 'thanks to X for partnering'), as stated in `description`, rather than the author's own topic with at most a passing tool mention?

newsjack.instructions: Is the post pegged to a product release or announcement that was new when it was posted (a new model, a new feature, a version number, 'just launched', 'just dropped'), judged from `title` and `description`?

tuning_notes: v1: generic lanes for B2B service companies. Rename the lanes or rewrite icp_fit for your niche; keep the off_niche label.
